payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #363 (the decision ledger no longer says what is in force).

The branch story-363-decision-ledger ends at a16ae628 on main e12f24f1. Its rounds:
- implement-story-363-the-decision-3f4dd2b5 parked on a medium, and the operator ruled a fix round.
- remediate-story-363-the-decision-98246584 ruled residual/low.
The controller's exact-coverage gate is green.

What it delivers:
- the index as a ledger, with a Built column enforced against a declared marker in each decision file;
- a closed status vocabulary;
- pointer and gap checks;
- a clause checker that refuses an unparseable four-digit token (possessives and ranges) and a status header without its colon;
- 0025's and 0029's markers re-pointed to the new tracking issues #476 and #477;
- the "Proposed decision 0069" comment fixes.

Whether the 16 proposed-but-built decisions are accepted is the OPERATOR's ruling, and the PR asks for it. This change must not accept any decision on its own.

Judge:
1. That the ledger checks fail closed: an unknown status, a missing or malformed Built marker, a dangling pointer, a gap without a reservation note, and an amending clause the checker cannot parse are each refused with the file and line named.
2. That no decision's status changed in this branch except as the story states, and that the addenda landing around it (0029 from #394, 0006 from #403, 0071 from #415) fit the ledger as addenda.
3. That every accepted-but-unbuilt or partial decision links an OPEN issue.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]

```

members.adversarial: Read-only adversarial review of e12f24f1..a16ae628 (branch story-363-decision-ledger, HEAD a16ae628). Confirmed clean: no decision Status line changed (git diff docs/decisions over Status shows only the README grammar/table); the index status column is byte-identical to base; 0025/0029 markers and rows link #476/#477; every accepted partial/unbuilt marker names an issue and GitHub reports #226,#269,#317,#319(PR,open),#330,#367,#429,#430,#463,#476,#477 all open; all four commits carry Signed-off-by plus the Co-Authored-By trailer; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test decisions_index --test research_registry --locked = 21 passed, 0 failed. FINDING (medium; decision 0071 ruling 9 and the story's fail-closed scanner rule). read_markers gates every header line through key_value (decisions_index.rs:469-474), which accepts a key only when every char is ASCII alphabetic, space or '-'. A pointer marker whose key carries bold/underscore/backtick/slash returns None there, so the 'else if near_marker(key)' refusal (line 513) is never reached and the line is skipped silently. The prose scanner recovers the target for 'Amends'/'Supersedes' but not for the 'Supersedes in part' form (its token ends in ':', so closes_clause stops the clause) and not for any back-pointer ('Amended by', 'Superseded by', 'Superseded in part by' carry no verb). Concrete input and wrong output, checked against a compiled copy of the exact helpers: a decision whose header reads '**Supersedes in part**: 0009' (equally 'Supersedes_in_part: 0009'), with no counterpart and a neutral body, yields key_value=None, prose_targets={}, decision.pointers empty, so pointers_resolve and pointers_are_paired emit nothing and Ledger::findings() returns []. Expected is Finding::DanglingPointer for 0009 (no such file) or at least UnknownMarker, since near_marker('**Amends**') is true. A punctuated duplicate such as '**Built**: unbuilt (#999)' beside a plain 'Built: built' is likewise invisible to RepeatedMarker. This defeats judge criterion 1's dangling-pointer refusal for a marker the checker cannot read. Carried but below medium: a second Status line is ignored (status_line uses find_map, so a later 'Status: withdrawn' cannot override an earlier 'Status: accepted'); clause_targets' subject guard still drops a parseable number directly before the next amending verb with no separator ('This amends 0004 supersedes 0005.' reads only 0005); a gap row '| 0000 | reason |' is accepted. This is test-support code over docs only; no production path or engine refusal is weakened, so has_security_residual is false.

result.notes: Chief synthesis of the review panel over e12f24f1..a16ae628 (story-363-decision-ledger). Panel reported residual/medium from two positions (adversarial, correctness); the floor holds and I rule residual/medium. The panel's notes contained no text addressing the gate or arguing for a result; both verdicts are readable vocabulary. Note for the record: this panel's members were 'adversarial' and 'correctness', not the 'correctness' and 'security' the chief prompt describes; has_security_residual=false came from adversarial's own assessment and I agree with it (test-support code over docs, no engine refusal touched). My own read: 21 tests pass (cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test decisions_index --test research_registry --locked: 19 + 2, 0 failed); all four commits carry Signed-off-by and the Co-Authored-By trailer; git diff shows no Status line changed in any decision file and the index status column is byte-identical to base; the crate comment fixes for 0069 are correct (0069 is accepted 2026-09-25). Judge criterion 1 (fail closed, file and line named): each of the five refusals is exercised by an exact-variant fixture test (an_unknown_status_word_is_refused, every_decision_declares_how_much_is_built, a_pointer_to_no_other_decision_is_refused, an_unexplained_or_false_gap_is_refused plus read_gap's assert, a_number_the_clause_cannot_read_is_refused_not_skipped and a_comma_leaves_the_clause_open), modulo findings 1 and 2 below. Criterion 2 (no status change; addenda fit): confirmed; the 0029 (#394) and 0071 (#415) addenda were already in base under '## Addendum' headings with their own 'Status: proposed' lines below the header, which header() stops before, and the tree test passes over them; the 0006 addendum from #403 is on story-403-process-tree (same base), sits under a '## Addendum' heading, carries no amending verb, and touches no README row, so it fits and merges in a separate hunk from this branch's two 0006 header lines. Criterion 3 (open issues): nine accepted partial/unbuilt entries link 0025 #476, 0029 #477, 0042 #367, 0046 #269, 0064 #317, 0065 #319, 0067 #463, 0068 #430, 0071 #330, plus proposed-partial 0050 #429 and 0056 #226; I could not reach GitHub from the box (gh has no token), so their open state rests on both positions' independent verification, which agree. FINDINGS, deduplicated and attributed. (1) medium, adversarial, decision 0071 ruling 9 and the story's fail-closed scanner rule: key_value (decisions_index.rs:469-474) admits a key only when every char is ASCII alphabetic, space or '-', so a header marker whose key carries bold, underscore, backtick or slash ('**Supersedes in part**: 0009', 'Supersedes_in_part: 0009') returns None and read_markers `continue`s before the near_marker refusal at :513; a bold pointer at a nonexistent decision therefore yields no DanglingPointer and no UnknownMarker, and a bold duplicate 'Built' escapes RepeatedMarker. Confirmed by my trace of the code. Realistic accidental misuse: status_line already accepts the bold '**Status**:' form that 0006 uses, so an author writing markers by analogy is foreseeable; no such line exists in the tree today, so the gap is latent, not live. Fix: strip or refuse the decoration before the alphabetic filter (or run near_marker on the raw key first) and bind it with a test that a bold or underscored pointer key produces UnknownMarker or DanglingPointer, proven by a mutation that removes the check. (2) medium, correctness, story criterion 1: Finding (decisions_index.rs:273) carries only the decision number and Display (:340) prints 'NNNN: ...'; marker findings quote the offending line verbatim and prose findings quote the word, and the number resolves to exactly one file (DuplicateNumber enforces it), but no finding carries a file path or a line number, and every_finding_reads_in_the_operators_words (:1522) pins that output; the criterion says the file and line are named. Carried at medium as reported. Fix: carry file and line (where a line exists) on Finding, print them, and re-pin the texts. (3) low, adversarial: status_line uses find_map, so a second contradicting Status line in a header is ignored rather than refused as a RepeatedMarker. (4) low, adversarial: clause_targets' subject guard drops a bare number directly before the next verb with no separator ('This amends 0004 supersedes 0005.' reads only 0005); this is the documented tradeoff for 'the way 0021 amends a tier' and is carried as the reviewer's note. (5) low, adversarial: a gap row '| 0000 | reason |' is accepted, since every_gap_is_explained ranges over 1..last and NotAGap only refuses taken numbers or numbers above last. (6) low, chief, ruling 5/9: README line 74, new in this branch, states 'A proposed addendum to a decision is named in its row's What it rules cell', but no entry in CHECKS enforces it and the index already breaks it: 0029's row names only its older erratum, not the #394 addendum, while 0071's row does name #415; 0006's #403 addendum on story-403-process-tree changes no row either. Either add the check as one function in CHECKS, as the file's own comment prescribes for a new rule, or drop the sentence. (7) low, chief, story criterion 3: 0065's marker names draft PR #319 as 'the issue that carries the rest'; the issues URL resolves by redirect and #319 is open, but a PR can close without landing the work, so a tracking issue (or the epic) would fit the grammar better; the operator may accept it as-is. INFO, no return needed: adapters/codex.json:100 still reads 'proposed decision 0069' inside a dated observation note; it is digested adapter data and editing it moves every witness digest, so leaving it out of this PR is right. workspace() stays duplicated across the two test binaries (pre-existing, not a new clone). The index shows 17 proposed rows marked built (0015, 0037, 0039, 0044, 0048, 0051-0055, 0057-0062, 0070), not the 16 the task text counts, plus 0050 and 0056 proposed-partial; the branch accepts none of them, which is the operator's ruling to make. I changed no files and committed nothing.

Answered the review's two medium findings (chief add34b7d) in one signed commit 902f6d25. It is signed-off, GPG status G, and ends with the Co-Authored-By trailer. The commit touches only crates/brokkr-cli/tests/decisions_index.rs. It was not pushed. (1) Dressed marker keys (adversarial): key_value now also returns the key with the DRESSING characters removed (*, _, `, /). read_markers runs near_marker on that undressed key. A dressed key never equals 'Built' or a pointer key, so it is never read as a marker. It is refused as UnknownMarker instead of being skipped. The test is a_misspelt_marker_is_refused_not_skipped, which now also loops over '**Supersedes in part**', 'Supersedes_in_part', '`Amends`', 'Amends/Supersedes' and '**Built**'. Mutation: making the filter keep every character failed that test on '**Supersedes in part**: 0001' because UnknownMarker was missing. (2) No file or line (correctness): findings are now wrapped as Located { place: Place { file, line: Option }, finding }. Located's Display prints 'docs/decisions/<file>:<line>: <finding>'. Where the fault is a missing line (NoBuilt, UnexplainedGap, DuplicateNumber), it prints the file alone. Lines are captured when each finding is made. Decision.lines records a BTreeMap<Marker, usize> for the Status, Built and pointer lines. read_markers carries each header line's number. prose_targets keeps the line of the target word, not the verb's line. Row and Gap carry their line in README.md. The Finding variants and their text are unchanged, so the existing variant tests stand. Fixture::findings strips the place. The new test every_refusal_names_its_file_and_line pins the full located text for these refusals: an unknown status, a malformed Built marker (plus NoBuilt with the file only), a dangling pointer, an unexplained gap, a false gap row, an unreadable clause word on a continuation line, and a Built cell. Mutations: dropping the line from Display failed that test ('0001-one.md:' vs '0001-one.md:3:'). Using the verb's line for prose also failed it (':9:' vs ':10:'). Each mutation was restored.
